title: Ops slab smoothing + salary curve sim (working sheet)
body:
Purpose: quick-run simulation sheet to test how hiring in time-slabs (3m hiring windows) + salary curve smoothing interacts with pricing sensitivity and GPU spot vs reserved mix. Use this to decide commit windows for Dedicated and burst buffer size. NOT a finalized plan; working assumptions and TODOs included.

Summary (one line): smoothing hires into 3 slabs lowers near-term burn by ~18% under base pricing assumptions but increases marginal token cost unless we compress slab-to-ops ramp faster.

Key assumptions:
- Baseline starting runway cash: $55,000,000 (cash + committed credit) as of 2026-11-01.
- Monthly token demand (billable): 12B tokens (aggregate across hosted & dedicated) in month 0. Growth base: +6%/mo; optimistic +10%/mo; downside +2%/mo.
- GPU ops cost (effective, includes infra/mgmt/overhead): reserved GPU pool cost per month: $1,200,000 per reserved cluster; spot mix unit cost per effective token: $0.0000016/token.
- Model mix: 60% medium large models (higher perf), 25% small, 15% experimental (quantized). Weighted cost per 1M tokens on baseline infra: $1.10 (including streaming overhead).
- Average comp (fully loaded) by role: Eng IC: $22k/mo, SRE: $24k/mo, Infra Eng: $26k/mo, Product/Design: $20k/mo. Contractors = 1.5x monthly rate per head.
- Hiring slabs: three 3-month slabs (Jan-Mar 27, Apr-Jun 27, Jul-Sep 27). In-slab hires ramp over the slab with linear onboarding (30% productivity first month, 65% second, 100% third month).
- Salary curve smoothing: we model two curves — sharp (all hires start at slab begin) and smoothed (evenly distributed across slab months).
- Pricing sensitivity: baseline net ARPU per 1M tokens = $2.50. Elasticity: for a -10% price change, demand +18% (cross-elastic); for +10% price change, demand -14%.

Scenario table (3 scenarios, 12-month look):

CSV_TABLE_HEADER: scenario,starting_runway_months,net_burn_mo_baseline,headcount_end_of_year,total_reserved_clusters,avg_price_per_1M_tokens,break_even_price_per_1M_tokens

Optimistic,24,$1,100,000,235,12,$2.80,$1.45
Base,18,$1,650,000,210,10,$2.50,$1.65
Downside,10,$2,350,000,190,8,$2.10,$2.05

Interpretation notes:
- "net_burn_mo_baseline" includes hired headcount comp, reserved cluster amortized cost, spot budget (variable), and ~10% corporate opex allocated.
- break_even_price_per_1M_tokens is the price required to get to non-negative contribution margin given modeled throughput and costs (not including long-term R&D).

Headcount slab example (Base scenario, total targeted hires 80 across year):
- Slab A (Q1): 30 hires: 18 Eng, 6 SRE, 4 Infra, 2 Product
- Slab B (Q2): 30 hires: 16 Eng, 8 SRE, 4 Infra, 2 Product
- Slab C (Q3): 20 hires: 12 Eng, 4 SRE, 2 Infra, 2 Product

Smoothing vs sharp compare (Base):
- Sharp: all Q1 salaries hit full comp by month 1 of Q1. Peak burn month (Mar) +14% vs smoothed.
- Smoothed: evenly split hires across months in slab. Peak burn reduced ~14% and average burn over 12 months reduced ~18% but gets more exposure to spot GPU unit costs because capacity comes online slower; this increases unit cost by ~6% compared to Sharp in base case.

Pricing sensitivity quick-sweep (Base):
- Price -15% (to $2.125/1M): demand +27% => token volume up, gross margin falls from 32% to ~18% unless ops improvements reduce cost per token by >15%.
- Price +15% (to $2.875/1M): demand -18% => immediate unit margin improves to ~40% but growth stalls; dedicated utilization drops and reserved amortization per effective token rises 12%.

Small worked example (Base, Month 6):
- Billable tokens month 6: 16.9B (growth from 12B).
- Ops cost (reserved + spot + ops) estimated = $1,750,000/mo.
- Headcount comp run-rate month 6: $1,150,000/mo (smoothed hires).
- Revenue at baseline price: (16.9B / 1M) * $2.50 = $42,250 -> wait units: that's $42,250k? Clarify: revenue = 16,900 * $2.50 = $42,250 (thousand dollars) => $42,250,000.
- Contribution margin = revenue - (ops + comp) = $42.25M - $2.9M = $39.35M (very healthy; note this is gross-hosting margin, other opex not included).

Risks and caveats (short):
- Model-mix shift towards larger models increases token-weighted ops cost nonlinearly; need per-route telemetry to detect.
- Under smoothed hiring, we may miss critical infra skills early and require contractors at premium (adds 20-30% comp pressure).
- Pricing elasticity numbers are noisy; propose running A/B tests on 10% price movements against matched cohorts (see linked_artifacts for JIRA).

Open action items (owner & estimate):
- Run per-route cost-of-serving analysis (Evan) — due 2026-11-30.
- Build 1-pager for exec: "slab smoothing tradeoffs" (Marcus) — due 2026-11-22.
- Simulate sensitivity with alternate elasticity priors (Priya) — due 2026-11-24.

Quick TODOs in sheet:
- Add column for contractor uplift by role and simulate 30% substitution in early slabs.
- Add regional price differentiation (EU vs US) and map to reserved cluster locations.
- Hook to product routing rules (A/B traffic to cheaper variants) and estimate short-term quality impact.

Notes to self:
- This file mixes high-level finance inputs with ops knobs; split into two sheets next pass: 1) Hiring & comp ledger, 2) Pricing sensitivity table + per-route cost.
- Keep a conservative reserve bucket (6 months) while experimenting with slab smoothing.
